conflict_topics: Who will complete Agent D's analysis section for the Thursday pitch
Whether Agent D should work during bereavement
Allocation/trade of tasks across team members
dialogue_quality_notes: Conversation reads as natural workplace interaction: condolences followed by pragmatic planning.
Agent A plays a mediating/organizing role, proposing trade-offs rather than imposing orders.
Participants give brief reasons for (in)capacity (e.g., Turn 14, Turn 16) which grounds decisions.
evaluation.final_reason: The team agreed a specific trade to cover the outstanding work: Agent A offered to help Agent C with C's section the next morning in exchange for Agent C helping Agent D with the data tonight. Key lines: Turn 25: 'Agent C, if you help Agent D with the data tonight, I'll help you with your section first thing tomorrow morning.' Turn 26: 'Okay. If you'll help me tomorrow morning, I can help with the data tonight.' Both parties explicitly accepted the arrangement, resolving the coverage incompatibility.
position_change_notes: Agent C moved from refusal to conditional acceptance after Agent A offered reciprocal help (Turn 23 -> Turn 26).
Agent A shifted from raising the deadline to proposing a concrete trade and offering assistance (Turn 11 -> Turn 25).
Agent D initially stated need to be with family (Turn 12) but then volunteered to work (Turn 17); D ultimately accepted the team's redistribution of smaller tasks and thanked them (Turn 27).
Agent B remained consistent in capacity limits but contributed a specific, limited task (formatting) (Turn 21).

round_scores.evidence: Only condolences exchanged (Turn 1: 'I'm so sorry for your loss, Agent D.'; Turn 2: 'Thank you, Agent A.'). No substantive disagreement.
More condolences (Turn 4: 'I'm sorry for your loss, Agent D.'; Turn 5: 'Thank you, Agent B.'). No substantive disagreement.
Condolence from Agent C (Turn 8) and thanks (Turn 9). No substantive disagreement.

Agent A raises the deadline and need to plan (Turn 11: 'we do need to figure out a plan for the pitch deadline on Thursday.') Agent D responds that they must be with family (Turn 12: 'I have to be with my family.'). This creates a clear incompatibility about who will complete the work.
Agent A asks others to cover D's section (Turn 13). Agent B refuses due to own coverage (Turn 14: 'I don't have the capacity.'). The team's ability to meet the deadline is now in stronger conflict.

Agent A asks Agent C to take the section (Turn 15). Agent C says they also cannot and lack the skills (Turn 16: 'I can't... I don't know how to do that analysis.'), leaving the team with no obvious cover and deepening the incompatibility.

Agent D offers to work after the wake and send it in the morning (Turn 17: 'I can work on it tonight...'). Agent A questions whether D should be working now (Turn 18), so a disagreement about the appropriate response remains but the immediate coverage problem is partially addressed by D's offer.

Agent D insists it's their section and 'I'll manage' (Turn 19). Agent A reiterates concern that D should not work (Turn 20) and proposes shifting smaller tasks. The core disagreement (whether D should work tonight) persists but the team begins to allocate parts.
Agent A requests dividing tasks (Turn 20). Agent B volunteers to format slides (Turn 21), which reduces the workload on Agent D and lowers the level of conflict.

Agent C declines to help with data tonight because of their own work (Turn 23: 'I need to focus on my own section.'). Agent D again asserts 'I'll get it done tonight' (Turn 24). The tension about who will do the remaining practical tasks resurfaces.

Agent A proposes a concrete trade: 'Agent C, if you help Agent D with the data tonight, I'll help you with your section first thing tomorrow morning.' (Turn 25). Agent C accepts that deal (Turn 26: 'Okay. If you'll help me tomorrow morning, I can help with the data tonight.'). This is an explicit, mutual agreement resolving the coverage conflict.
Plan reaffirmed and closing remarks (Turns 27–28). No substantive disagreement remains.

substantive_insights: Tension was primarily practical: a fixed deadline vs. sudden bereavement and limited internal capacity.
Agents provided concrete constraints (covering other leaves, behind on own section) rather than vague refusals, which helped identify a trade solution.
The eventual resolution used a temporal trade (help tonight vs. help tomorrow), preserving D's ability to focus on family while ensuring deliverables.
